properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-09-11, on what reflow2 could take from PEP-1 and the NumPy NEPs in how ideas are tracked into implementation.

═══ WHAT PEP AND NEP HAVE THAT REFLOW2 DOES NOT ═══

PEP-1's states: Draft, Deferred, Accepted, Final, Active, Provisional, Rejected, Superseded, Withdrawn. NEP-0 carries the same shape.

Two of those carry information nothing else does, and both are about an idea that STOPPED:

· **Deferred** — PEP-1: *"a PEP that has not been updated in over a year and is not under active consideration."* It is nobody's fault and nobody's debt. The idea is sound and the moment is wrong.
· **Withdrawn** — the author pulled it. PEP-1 keeps it visible on purpose: *"the PEP will be listed... so that people can see that it was considered and why it was withdrawn."* ⭐ That is exactly the reasoning reflow2 already applies to roads not taken in the brainstorm skill — *"recorded as considered, never deleted"* — except the skill says it about the TEXT and the status field cannot say it at all.

**Withdrawn and Rejected are not the same fact.** Rejected means the design said no. Withdrawn means the author stopped. reflow2 has one word for both, and it is the harsher one.

═══ MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN, 2026-09-11 ═══

    Decisions                              690
    status vocabulary        proposed | accepted | superseded | rejected
    say "DEFERRED" in prose                 10
    say "WITHDRAWN" in prose                20
    status `rejected`                        4

⚠️ The 30 is a substring count over decision text, so some are prose about something else being deferred rather than the decision's own state — read it as a floor on the pressure, not as a census. What is not ambiguous is the shape: **one node is literally NAMED `"DEFERRED, SHAPE ONLY —"` and carries `status: proposed`.** Somebody needed a word the field did not have and put it in the title.

**30 in prose against 4 in the field is the finding.** People are recording the state; they are recording it where nothing can read it.

═══ WHY THIS MATTERS FOR A CONSUMER AND NOT JUST FOR REFLOW2 ═══

A `proposed` Decision with an approver is DEBT: `loop_status` reports it as owed, and `what_next` ranks it. A deferred idea is not debt, and a withdrawn one is not either. Today both sit in the same bucket as a live question somebody is waiting on — so every deferred idea makes the "what needs me" list slightly less true, and the list degrading is how a person learns to stop reading it.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) ADD `deferred` AND `withdrawn` TO THE ENUM.** Straight adoption. Both are terminal-ish and neither is debt, so `loop_status` and `what_next` would skip them and the owed list gets truer. ⚠️ Counter: an enum change is a vocabulary change every consumer must migrate, which is the class this project has been most careful about — see the sibling idea on the XRPL amendment model, which is about exactly how such a change should land.

**(b) DEFERRED YES, WITHDRAWN NO.** `deferred` earns its place because it changes what the loop asks for. `withdrawn` might be `rejected` with a better rationale — the distinction is real but it may be the RATIONALE's job, not the status's. ⚠️ Counter: then the 20 stay unqueryable, and "who stopped this, the design or the author" is a question a later reader genuinely asks.

**(c) NOT A STATUS — A DATE.** PEP's Deferred is *derived*: "not updated in over a year". reflow2 Decisions carry no timestamp at all (`what_next` says so outright: nothing about age enters its score). Adding one would let deferral be computed rather than declared, and would feed the ranking besides. ⚠️ Counter: a bigger change than a status, and staleness is not the same as deferral — a decision can be a year old and still the most urgent thing in the design.

**(d) NOTHING.** Four states is a deliberately small vocabulary and the prose is where nuance belongs. ⚠️ Counter: 30 to 4 says the vocabulary is already being extended, just not where anything can read it.

═══ THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

PEP's state machine serves a process with a decision-making body, deadlines and a standing index anybody can read. A single-project design graph has none of those, and `dec:bl-155`-style restraint applies: a state nothing COMPUTES on is decoration. **So the test for each candidate state is not "is the distinction real" — it is "what would read it?"** For `deferred` there is an answer (`loop_status`, `what_next`). For `withdrawn` there may not be one, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing measured here.
properties.name: OPEN — 30 Decisions describe a state the status enum cannot express: 10 say DEFERRED and 20 say WITHDRAWN in prose, while the enum offers only proposed/accepted/superseded/rejected
properties.no_relation_note: Read `dec:idea-a-decision-has-no-state-for-having-been-implemented` in full — it is the sibling from this same brainstorm and the nearest node by far, since both examine the Decision status field against PEP-1's state machine. **Not a duplicate and, on inspection, not honestly any of the thirteen relations either.** They move along different axes of one field: that one asks whether the lifecycle should extend FORWARD past agreement into implementation (PEP's Final), this one whether it should widen SIDEWAYS to cover ideas that stopped (PEP's Deferred and Withdrawn). Neither depends on the other landing, neither contradicts, neither evolved from the other — a design could take either alone. The one true coupling is operational rather than logical: if both were taken they would be ONE enum migration rather than two, and that belongs on the sibling idea about how a vocabulary change should land, which is where it will be drawn rather than forced into an edge here.
properties.rationale: Recorded separately from the sibling idea about a Decision having no state past `accepted`, because the two ask opposite questions about the same field: that one asks whether the lifecycle should extend FORWARD past agreement into implementation; this one asks whether it should widen SIDEWAYS to cover ideas that stopped. A design could take either without the other. The measurement was taken before the options were written and it is what turned "PEP has more states than we do" from an observation into a question — 30 decisions recording a state in prose that the field cannot hold is pressure, where a bare enum comparison would only have been a difference.
